record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional Berger sphere with mu > 1, the Hopf unit vector field is not energy-minimizing because there are unit vector fields in the two-dimensional span generated by the orthogonal fields E1 and E2 with smaller energy. Which unit vector fields actually minimize the energy functional in this case?

evidence.quote: for all unit vector fields X in the 2-dimensional space generated by .{E1 , E2 }
we don’t know if these vector fields are the minimisers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3$ denote the 3-sphere equipped with the Berger metric $g_\mu$ obtained by canonical variation of the Hopf fibration: starting from the round metric of constant sectional curvature 1, rescale the metric along the Hopf direction by a positive parameter $\mu$, so that, with respect to a global orthonormal frame $\{E_1,E_2,V\}$ where $V$ is tangent to the Hopf fibers (the Hopf unit vector field) and $E_1,E_2$ span the horizontal distribution of the Hopf fibration, the Berger metric satisfies $g_\mu(V,V)=\mu^2$, $g_\mu(E_i,E_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $g_\mu(V,E_i)=0$. For a smooth unit vector field $X$ on $(S^3,g_\mu)$, define its energy by
$$E(X)\;=\;\tfrac12\int_{S^3}\bigl(n+\|\nabla X\|^2\bigr)\,\mathrm{dvol}_{g_\mu},$$
where $n=3$ and $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g_\mu$.

It is known that for $\mu>1$ the Hopf unit vector field $V$ is not a minimizer of $E$ on the space of unit vector fields, since one can find unit vector fields lying in the 2-dimensional horizontal distribution spanned by $E_1,E_2$ that have strictly smaller energy than $V$.

Problem: For each $\mu>1$, determine explicitly the unit vector field(s) on the Berger 3-sphere $(S^3,g_\mu)$ that minimize the energy functional $E$ among all smooth unit vector fields, and compute the corresponding minimum value of $E$.
artifact.category_tag: Energy of unit vector fields on Berger spheres
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature studies the stability of Hopf vector fields on Berger spheres and shows their instability with respect to energy when μ>1, but does not identify the actual energy minimizers. The problem of explicitly characterizing the energy minimizers on Berger 3-spheres for μ>1 appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Volume, energy and generalized energy of unit vector fields on Berger spheres: stability of Hopf vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: study to what extent the known results concerning the behaviour of Hopf vector fields, with respect to volume, energy and generalized energy functionals, on the round sphere are still valid for the metrics obtained by performing the canonical variation of the Hopf fibration
status_evidence.claim: This paper studies stability (not identification of minimizers) of Hopf vector fields on Berger spheres.

status_evidence.title: Unit vector fields of minimum energy on quotients of spheres and stability of the Reeb vector field
status_evidence.snippet: unit Hopf vector fields are the unique unit vector fields which minimize the energy
status_evidence.claim: Minimizers known on quotients of round spheres, not on Berger spheres with μ>1.
